# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

I read the code for all four main pages (/, /pricing, /docs, /blog), plus the layout, `robots.txt`, the sitemap and `geo.config.json`. I treated /thank-you as deliberately hidden and left it out of the route counts. Nothing was unknown, so the range is a single number. This is a score read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a language to the page
- **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells search engines, AI tools and screen readers what language your pages are in. Without it, they have to guess.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100 (use `<html lang="en">`; `geo.config.json` already says `"language": "en"`)

### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Your sitemap lists your pages for crawlers. `robots.txt` is the first place crawlers look, and it doesn't mention the sitemap.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: GPTBot` / `Disallow: /` (the file ends here with no `Sitemap:` line)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 78/100 (add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`). Fixing items 1 and 2 together gives 86/100.

### 3. Make /pricing indexable and keep its canonical consistent
- **Why it matters:** /pricing is in your sitemap and navigation, but it tells search engines not to index it. Its canonical tag also points at that same excluded page. If this is unintended, a key page is hidden from search and AI search.
- **Where:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`
- **Size:** Small. Confirm the noindex isn't deliberate first. If it is, remove /pricing from `public/sitemap.xml:4` instead.
- **Score after this:** 77/100 if you remove the noindex. A deliberate noindex would instead need the sitemap entry removed.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says they should | Clear | `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /`. GPTBot is blocked, which matches `trainingCrawlers: block` |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | /pricing is noindex (`app/pricing/page.tsx:1`). 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the site's own origin | Problem | Missing on /docs and /blog. /pricing points at a noindex page. Only / is clear (1 of 4) |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` loads posts in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap that is discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang`. Titles and descriptions are present on every route |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are linked with real links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13` uses `<a href>` for all four pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Only `data-nosnippet` on the cookie notice (`app/layout.tsx:15`), which is a deliberate scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Selected accessibility checks | Clear | Read the layout and all pages: no images, and every link has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | No `llms.txt`; never scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app; never scored |

## Other problems found

- **The blog's data source doesn't exist in this repository.** `app/blog/page.tsx:8` has `fetch('/api/posts')`, but there is no `app/api` route. The blog will probably always render empty. Add the route or load the posts on the server.

## Worth considering

- **Blog posts as pages:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `posts.map((p) => <article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>)`. Each post could have its own page at an address like `/blog/<slug>`, listed in the sitemap, so it can be found and quoted individually.
- **Pricing page copy:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has the description `Plans for every team size.`, but the page says only `Free for up to three people.` Adding the paid plans, prices and limits as text would make the page match what it promises.
- **Docs depth:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has the description `How to set up Ledger.`, but the page is one sentence: `Start by importing your bank feed.` Steps for setup, supported banks and importing would answer what a visitor comes to ask.
- **Home page links:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` The page names three features but links to none. Linking to /docs or a feature page would help readers and crawlers move on.
- **Titles that name the site:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has `title: 'Docs'` and `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `title: 'Pricing'`. In a results list, "Docs | Ledger" says whose docs they are. A title template in `app/layout.tsx:5` would do this.
- **Site identity as structured data:** I found no Organization or WebSite JSON-LD. The name "Ledger" and the origin `https://www.ledger.example` are already declared, so you could add them as a label for machines.
- **Sitemap dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no `<lastmod>` on any entry. Adding dates, especially for blog posts once they exist, shows crawlers what changed.
- **Generated sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml` is hand-written. Next.js can generate it from `app/sitemap.ts`, so new pages like blog posts get listed without manual edits.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** a live scan would confirm that the sitemap URLs return 200 and that no `X-Robots-Tag` header is set outside the repository.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site. `geo.config.json` says `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`.
- The noindex on /pricing is unintended, because the page is in the sitemap and the main navigation. /thank-you is intentionally noindexed.
- /thank-you is a deliberately hidden page, so I excluded it from the route counts.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
